consentTypes.name: Building Consent
consentTypes.description: Required before starting most building work, including new builds, alterations, additions, and some maintenance. Ensures work meets the New Zealand Building Code.
consentTypes.whoNeedsIt: Anyone undertaking building work that is not exempt under the Building Act 2004.
consentTypes.feeNotes: Fees are based on the value of the building work. A minimum lodgement fee applies. Additional inspection fees may apply.
requiredDocuments: Certificate of Title or proof of ownership

consentTypes.name: Resource Consent
consentTypes.description: Required when your proposed activity doesn't comply with the Nelson Resource Management Plan. Covers land use, subdivision, and effects on the environment.
consentTypes.whoNeedsIt: Anyone undertaking activities that require consent under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA) or the Nelson Resource Management Plan.
consentTypes.feeNotes: Initial lodgement deposit required. Actual costs charged on a time and cost basis. Complex or notified consents cost significantly more.
requiredDocuments: Application form with assessment of environmental effects (AEE)
Written approval from affected neighbours (if applicable)

consentTypes.name: LIM Report (Land Information Memorandum)
consentTypes.description: A document issued by the council containing information about a property known to the council — including consents, notices, zoning, and any special features or hazards.
consentTypes.whoNeedsIt: Buyers, property owners, developers, and anyone wanting a full picture of a property's history and requirements.
consentTypes.feeNotes: Standard fee applies. Urgent LIMs may incur additional charges if offered.

consentTypes.name: Certificate of Acceptance
consentTypes.description: Issued for building work carried out without a building consent (e.g. urgent work or work that pre-dates consent requirements). It confirms the council has inspected the work and it complies with the Building Code as far as can be determined.
consentTypes.whoNeedsIt: Anyone who needs to legalise building work done without a consent, typically during property sale or when refinancing.
consentTypes.feeNotes: Fees similar to building consents. Council may refuse if the work cannot be inspected adequately.
requiredDocuments: Any existing consents or documentation for the work
Producer Statements from tradespeople if available

consentTypes.name: Building Consent
consentTypes.description: Required before starting most building work, including new builds, alterations, additions, and some maintenance. Ensures work meets the New Zealand Building Code.
consentTypes.whoNeedsIt: Anyone undertaking building work that is not exempt under the Building Act 2004.
consentTypes.feeNotes: Tasman uses a fee schedule based on project value. Lodgement fees, inspection fees, and processing fees all apply.
requiredDocuments: Site plan (to scale) showing property boundaries

consentTypes.name: Resource Consent
consentTypes.description: Required when your proposed activity doesn't comply with the Tasman Resource Management Plan. Covers land use, subdivision, coastal activities, and environmental effects.
consentTypes.whoNeedsIt: Anyone undertaking activities requiring consent under the RMA or the Tasman Resource Management Plan.
consentTypes.feeNotes: Deposit required upfront. Full costs charged on time and expense basis. Notify Tasman DC early for complex applications.
requiredDocuments: Resource consent application form with AEE

consentTypes.name: LIM Report (Land Information Memorandum)
consentTypes.description: A document issued by the council containing information about a property — including consents issued, rates, zoning, hazards, and any special classifications or notices.
consentTypes.whoNeedsIt: Buyers, owners, developers, and anyone wanting comprehensive information about a property's history.
consentTypes.feeNotes: Standard fee. Check Tasman DC website for the current fee schedule.

consentTypes.name: Certificate of Acceptance
consentTypes.description: For building work carried out without a consent or where an existing consent cannot be amended. The council inspects the completed work and issues a certificate if it substantially complies with the Building Code.
consentTypes.whoNeedsIt: Property owners who need to regularise unconsented building work, often required when selling.
consentTypes.feeNotes: Fees are assessed on a case-by-case basis similar to building consent fees.
